![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/97faa2ca35485f76f012475a9ba2b6af7938cfc86728bddd560cf3da59fff197.png)

Which of the diagrams above shows three collinear points?
question.worked_solution:
Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn.

- Diagram I shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/f52592db0fee86e26318d6d2de9d7f685f1fb9f5d416628a04878857f1c54b54.png)

- Diagram II shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/76f0da764caf0237a2d30d32d593886d8df6c348368fe889f7447be781b6faf1.png)

- Diagram III shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/9778abd955cdc9b705800eba8f3d0d635af1c6a5fd5724583bdb32a943c6d44f.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
